title: Average Treatment Effects with Jointly Chart-Reviewed Treatment and Outcome under Vanishing Review Probability
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded subfield below the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4; the stylized review design and absent practical evidence limit breadth despite sound matched MSE and honest-length results.
gap_reasons: The theorem is confined to a one-dimensional uniform score, a known exact power-law review mechanism, known beta and fixed kappa, so it does not establish a general weak-overlap or estimated-review-design frontier.

Its honest interval is a conservative Markov enlargement: matching expected-length order does not provide sharp constants, law-specific calibration, or the studentized inference discussed as the remaining objective.

The projected paper score is limited by this stylized design scope and the absence of evidence showing that the theoretical gains materially affect realistic chart-review planning, not by an unproved step in the headline theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery note derived matched minimax MSE and honest connected-interval expected-length orders, including the critical logarithm, and passed the D0.5 math and decision reviews. Formalization reached an F2 scaffold and F2.5 source audit, which prompted a narrow repair of the unconsumed Mou citation; F3-F5 and final Lean verification were not completed. After that repair, the novelty review graded the sound result subfield below the fixed field floor because the design remained stylized and practical impact was not demonstrated.
tldr: Gold-standard treatment and binary outcome may both require manual chart review even when a review score and baseline code are observed for every record. Under the public design \(q_{\kappa}(u)=u^{\kappa}/2\), the main theorem constructs a total shell-adaptive histogram and an explicit finite-sample connected interval that use \(\beta\) and \(\kappa\) but neither the propensity \(e\) nor its smoothness \(\eta\). Uniformly over \(\eta\in[1/4,1]\), they attain root risk and honest expected length \(\sqrt{\log(eN)/N}\) at \(\kappa=1\) and \(N^{-(\beta+1)/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\) for fixed \(\kappa>1\); a common constant-propensity subclass supplies matching all-procedure converses even when \(e\) is supplied. Relative to the accepted-bank discrete random-label ATE annotation frontier, this is a score-dependent joint-review observation experiment over a Hölder response class rather than a discrete random-label experiment, and it additionally matches honest connected-interval length as well as MSE. Mou et al. study a different one-arm local Sobolev MSE problem; we compare only the displayed powers and invoke no class-inclusion transfer. The contribution is the global joint-review Hölder experiment, its observable finite-sample certificate and honest-length frontier, and the eta-adaptive no-propensity-penalty conclusion.
gap: Hou, Mukherjee, and Cai study jointly unobserved treatment and response under random labeling and derive regular semi-supervised efficiency theory. Mou et al. derive smoothness-dependent weak-overlap phases in an RKHS observation model. Neither paper proves a same-class original-data minimax and honest-length frontier for spatially vanishing joint review with unknown bounded treatment propensity.
fill: A shell-adaptive histogram controls conditional category counts, empty bins, review-probability variation within bins, and reuse of records in coarse and fine terms. A public squared-risk certificate yields finite-sample honesty, while same-class two-point alternatives certify both minimax MSE and connected-interval expected-length lower bounds in the more informative known-propensity experiment.
